summary: San Miguel County site listed under the Santa Fe NF; a 1989 survey photo dated 1937 shows an L-4 or L-5 log lookout house, probably built in the early to mid 1930s; FFLA lists the site as gone.

facts.design: L-4 or L-5 log lookout house (photographed 1937; survey caption says it probably was built in the early to mid 1930s)
facts.status_note: FFLA lists the site as gone, with no date; no account of its removal found

events.note: Photograph date from the 1989 survey caption; a photo date, not a build date. The same caption gives a probable build range of the early to mid 1930s.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only evidence beyond FFLA is a 1989 survey photo caption (Figure 43) that gives no dated build record and no builder, but says the house probably was constructed in the early to mid 1930s. The survey has no Rosilla section. The Forest Lookouts Rosilla page shows only the name and agency. The FFLA New Mexico pages link a document titled 'Fire Lookout History of the Santa Fe National Forest'; it was not located or opened and is the best next lead. Two WebSearch calls were used; one NRHP result was for Glorieta Baldy, not Rosilla, and was not used.
